chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

“The sun declines in the middle of Ḥazīrān by half a foot; in the middle of Tammūz by one and a half feet; in the middle of Āb by two and a half feet; in the middle of Aylūl by three and a half feet; in the middle of Tishrīn al-Awwal by five and a half feet; in the middle of Tishrīn al-Ākhir by seven and a half feet; in the middle of Kānūn al-Awwal by nine and a half feet; in the middle of Kānūn al-Ākhir by seven and a half feet; in the middle of Shubāṭ by five and a half feet; in the middle of Ādhār by three and a half feet; in the middle of Naysān by two and a half feet; in the middle of Ayyār by one and a half feet; and in the middle of Ḥazīrān by half a foot.”

key_terms.أَقْدَامٍ: feet, a plural measure of length
key_terms.النِّصْفِ: the middle point of the month
key_terms.تِشْرِينَ الْأَوَّلِ: Tishrīn al-Awwal, the month of October
key_terms.حَزِيرَانَ: Ḥazīrān, the month of June in the Syriac calendar
key_terms.قَدَمٍ: a foot-length as a unit of measure
key_terms.كَانُونَ الْأَوَّلِ: Kānūn al-Awwal, the month of December

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the sun’s decline through the months of the year?
ai.summary: This hadith records measured positions for the sun’s decline at the middle of each month of the solar year. Its significance is in helping determine the seasonal variation relevant to recognizing zawāl, especially in the context of prayer-time reckoning.
